topic: Retain original historical visit identities before object deletion
sourceTrace: Private enteredActors retains object references, while actorVisits is keyed by netId recorded at observation. The version2 room serializer rejected null entered references and derived all IDs from current objects, so a deleted historical entrant prevented capture.

Physical observation adds enteredActors and keyed visits only after existing inside/same-floor/segment checks. Current resume reconstructs visits only from exact group/episode/node receipts for available original actors. These two points can retain original identity before later deletion.
implementation: Add private enteredActorIdentities rows[originalActor,originalNetId] at first qualified physical entry and valid historical receipt adoption. Keep rows aligned with enteredActors. The existing pushBackUnique pass determines first entry by array length change; no second membership scan.

Room serializer version3/thirteen fields appends identity rows. Require at most64 rows aligned with enteredActors; unique nonempty original IDs exactly matching visit-map keys. A surviving object must still have that ID. A null original object can retain its historical string key; it never resolves to another object.

Preserve every original unique room index only within shared physically cleared coverage, exact ordered positions/visit context and original budgets/clocks. Copy row arrays; do not infer missing identities at transfer time or copy another actor's observations to a replacement.
Outer private capture becomes version6, still twelve fields, requiring the13-field room component. No public receipt schema, native command, worker, clock or incoming consumer changes.
cost: One small private identity row per first physical entrant or admitted historical actor, using the existing uniqueness scan. Capture validates/copies at most64 identity rows in addition to existing room histories. No extra periodic callback, world query, timer or network message. Actual5percent median/10percent p95 remains unmeasured.
limits: Only identities recorded before deletion survive. Missing/malformed legacy identity rows refuse; no reconstruction from null objects or nearby replacements.

Current lane/egress actor suitability and original native/settings proof still apply. An unavailable/deleted active worker can still fail those other component checks; this is not complete casualty replacement or deletion handover.
Incoming authoritative replay remains absent. Existing legacy resume only reconstructs receipts for currently admitted available actors; this change does not silently consume the new private capture.
Follow-through/early-exit/reserve domains, motion/settings/interruption/retirement, authenticated producer seal/request replay and actual native readiness remain incomplete.
Physical normal/HC/Zeus/repeat behaviour, casualty refill, balance and performance unverified; audits paused.
